summary: Kevin A. Vose works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his BA at Bates College (1992) and an MA (1999) and PhD (2005) at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins and Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, Kevin Buckelew studied at Sarah Lawrence College and Columbia University (PhD 2018) under supervisors Ch''''ün-fang Yü, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang. In 2018, he became Assistant Professor at Northwestern University.

Kevin Vogelaar focuses on history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at SUNY New Paltz (BA 2014), Fordham (MA 2018), and Tufts (MA 2020), he held posts at Fordham, Tufts (2019–2020), and the Armenian Museum of America (2020).
Kexin Zheng specializes in Indology and religious studies. As attested in 2026, Zheng is a PhD candidate at Leiden University studying under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop.

Khakyab Dorje (1871–1922) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamg''''ön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye (1887–1888), Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Khenchen Tashi ''''Özer, Tsuklak Nyinjé, Mingyur Wanggyel, and Sheja Künkhyen, and taught numerous students.
Kham Sum Ziln''''ön Gyepa Dorj''''é studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Ch''''ökyi Lodr''''ö.

Khammai Dhammasami (b. 1965) earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (~2000–2004). He founded Oxford Buddha Vihara (serving as abbot ~2003) and Shan State Buddhist University (2014), and held posts at ITBMU, OCBS, and Oxford.
An Indologist, Khanderao Deshpande studied under doctoral supervisor Moriz Winternitz. He served as Joint Director at Osmania University, attested in 1969.
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk (1938–2014) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.
Khen Gen Jampal Dorj''''é studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Khenchen Ngawang Khyen Rab Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche (1938–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries and under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche, he chaired the Nyingma section at CIHTS (~1967–1984).
Khenchen Tashi ''''Özer studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamg''''ön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye. His students included Khakyab Dorje and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (1933–2023) studied under Khenpo Gangshar and the 16th Karmapa. An expert in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he was abbot of Rumtek (~1968), Karma Shri Nalanda (~1981), and Gampo Abbey (~1984–2023).
Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Khenpo Appey Rinpoche (1927–2010), a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at Dzongsar Monastery and under Drakgyab Lodr''''ö. He served at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and directed Sakya College from 1972 to 1985.
Khenpo Dazer, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima. He served as a teacher at both Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and Œrī Siṃha Shedra.

Khenpo Gangshar (1925–1980) studied at Shechen Monastery under Shechen Kongtrul, Khyentse Ozer, and Kars''''é Kongtrul. A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, he taught at Shechen and was founding dean of Surmang Monastery (~1957–1958).

Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok (1933–2004) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima, Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Ch''''ö Pel, Khenchen Dazer, and several other teachers, mentoring many students.

Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (1924–2019) studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1958) and under Khenpo Gangshar, the 8th Traleg Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he taught at Rumtek (1967) and founded/led KTD (1978).
